```json
{"action": "refine",
 "reason": "Power (144 vs 140 uW) is mostly the resistor current, so lowering vout_t and I fixes it. Swing is barely sensitive to any current variable. Vdsat (subthreshold Vov) is set by Vth at the fixed 0.75 V bias, so widening the L ranges lets the search look for higher-Vth or weaker-inversion sizing.",
 "params": {"I": 50e-6, "Ln": 0.5, "Lp": 0.5, "R": 11e3, "vout_t": 0.82},
 "bounds": {"I": [35e-6, 58e-6], "Ln": [0.15, 2.0], "Lp": [0.15, 2.0], "R": [8e3, 13e3], "vout_t": [0.76, 1.0]}}
```

This only tests a guess about the swing. Power should fix itself: Ip drops from about 70 µA to about 58 µA, and the budget allows 67.8 µA. GBW and the -3 dB bandwidth still have margin.

The swing is the problem I can't explain yet. The sensitivities show it hardly responds to I or R. That points to a floor set by each device's Vdsat, and at a fixed 0.75 V gate bias Vdsat depends on Vth. Here I'm assuming Vth in SKY130 changes enough with channel length to matter, so I've widened the L range to 0.15–2 µm.

If swing still stays near 1.41 V, the guess was wrong. I'll then edit the topology so the gates are not pinned to the input DC level and the devices can sit in deeper weak inversion.
